title: Dialzara alternatives: 8 Best options for 2026
summary: Looking for Dialzara alternatives? These eight options offer better scalability and flexibility, plus more advanced features.
body_markdown:
Maybe you’re here because you’re using Dialzara and looking for an alternative. Or maybe your current provider doesn’t offer many features for missed calls, and you’re wondering whether Dialzara can meet your needs.


Dialzara is an AI-powered phone answering service that supports outbound voice, web chat, and SMS. It starts at a relatively low price of $29 per month. But it isn’t a dedicated business phone system. Many past users also struggled with per-minute billing and overage charges. That’s why they often switch to less expensive platforms.


Here’s how the top Dialzara alternatives stack up:


- [Sona](https://www.quo.com/sona) , by Quo, is the best Dialzara alternative for small and growing businesses that want a built-in business phone system.
- **Ruby Receptionist** is the best Dialzara alternative for live receptionists instead of AI.
- **Retell AI** is the best Dialzara alternative for healthcare teams that need HIPAA compliance.
- **My AI Front Desk** is the best Dialzara alternative with an email AI agent.
- **Ringly** is the best Dialzara alternative for ecommerce companies with a Shopify store.


In this article, you can compare the pros and cons of eight Dialzara alternatives. You’ll see why businesses switch from Dialzara. Then, you’ll learn what to prioritize when choosing an alternative.


##


**8 Best Dialzara alternatives + pricing and why they beat Dialzara**


You might be tempted by Dialzara’s price tag. But is it *really* the best option for your growing small business? Or will the costs catch up with you later?


Compare the providers below and come to your own conclusion.

- Uses an interactive demo to help you set up in minutes

- Transfers complex calls to humans


#### Cons


- Like any AI receptionist, Sona requires fine-tuning after launch


**Where it beats Dialzara:** Sona charges per call, which keeps costs predictable compared to Dialzara’s per-minute calls. You won’t have to force your AI to end calls without resolution to save money. Plus, Sona takes calls on your phone system. It also keeps records in the same contact thread as your team’s calls and texts.


Sona is an[AI voice agent](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/voice-agent) that’s built into Quo — the best business phone system for small and growing businesses. It’s not a third-party answering service that takes forwarded calls like Dialzara. That means you can use Sona in the same system you use to make calls and send texts.


Your team won’t have to manage two separate tools for call histories or forward calls to a third-party answering system. Instead, you’ll get a[full conversation history](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/inboxes/overview) for calls, texts, voicemails, and recordings. You can easily save time following up on conversations in Quo’s[call views](https://www.quo.com/blog/introducing-sona/) .

- Answer FAQs to save time for callers and your team

- Transfer calls to humans in the case of an escalation or emergency

You can also use Quo’s call flow builder to choose *how* and *when* Sona picks up the phone. For example, you could use Sona for backup[call routing](https://www.quo.com/product/call-routing) . That means you’d create a call flow that rings your receptionist first, then your staff in a[ring group](https://www.quo.com/features/ring-groups) , then defaults to Sona as a fallback option.


Since Sona is natively built into a business phone system, you can easily integrate it with the tools you already use. For example, you can connect Quo to a CRM like[Clio](https://www.quo.com/integrations/clio) ,[Jobber](https://www.quo.com/integrations/jobber) , or[HubSpot](https://www.quo.com/integrations/hubspot) to log transcripts and summaries in your contacts field. This makes it easy to move data without manually entering caller information. Use a CRM that’s not on this list? Use[Zapier](https://www.quo.com/integrations/zapier) and[Make](https://www.quo.com/integrations/make) to connect with another system in your stack.


For all these reasons and many more, 90,000 businesses rely on Quo to build better customer relationships.

### **2. Smith.ai: Best Dialzara alternative with live human backup**


#### Pros


- Escalates complex or high-value calls to live receptionists
- Create custom call-handling playbooks for different callers
- Send instant call summaries to Slack or Microsoft Teams


#### Cons


- No built-in business phone system
- High costs for limited call volumes
- Call recording and transcriptions are only stored for 90 days
- Steep overage rates


**Where it beats Dialzara:** Smith.ai charges per call rather than per minute. It also offers a free entry plan for up to 25 AI calls per month. Plus, it has native CRM integrations with platforms like Jobber and[Housecall Pro](https://www.quo.com/integrations/housecall-pro) .


Smith.ai is a hybrid receptionist that can answer calls with AI *or* human receptionists. You can choose between AI-first, human-first, or hybrid handling. All plans come with the same basic features: caller greetings, answering FAQs, and transferring calls elsewhere when needed.


💡 **Learn more** about[AI receptionists versus human receptionists](https://www.quo.com/blog/ai-receptionist-vs-human-receptionist/) .


AI-first plans include exclusive features like AI scheduling via Calendly. You’ll also have native and third-party CRM integrations for automatically logging caller information.


For human-first plans, you get support for lead qualification and new client intake forms. Want features like Spanish support or call recordings and transcriptions? A dedicated Spanish number costs an extra $1 per call, and recordings and transcriptions cost $0.25 extra per call. Even the human answering service appointment-scheduling feature costs extra.


You can also choose a hybrid plan where both AI and humans answer calls. Pricing depends on the setup you choose and how often calls need human support. Two common setups are:


- **Humans for new clients, AI for existing ones** . Receptionists handle new leads and intake. The AI takes calls from people you already work with.
- **Humans during business hours, AI after hours** . Receptionists answer while you’re open. The AI takes calls when you’re closed.


Keep in mind that Smith AI caps you at around 34 calls per day. But to access that number of calls, you’ll need the top tier of the Enterprise plan. Prices start at $800 a month — a high cost compared to other[Smith.ai alternatives](https://www.quo.com/blog/smith-ai-alternatives/) .

### **3. Ruby Receptionist: Best for offices that want human receptionists**


#### Pros


- 24/7 live US-based human receptionists on every plan
- Provides support in English and Spanish


#### Cons


- Per-minute pricing can get expensive
- Call quality can vary between receptionists
- No native integration with platforms like Jobber or ServiceTitan


**Where it beats Dialzara:** Ruby’s human receptionists can handle nuanced, sensitive, or emotional calls. Ruby offers HIPAA compliance and bilingual receptionists available on the base plan.


Ruby is a live[virtual receptionist](https://www.quo.com/product/virtual-receptionist) service that supports your business with US-based staff. Live reps can take messages, qualify leads, and transfer calls for you 24/7. There are also plans available for live web chat services. That way, your website visitors can connect with Ruby receptionists to ask questions and get answers without having to pick up the phone.


That said, Ruby *only* offers human receptionists. It doesn’t support AI agents, even as a backup option. That means it can get expensive fast.For example: 500 minutes of handled calls costs $1,725 per month. That’s far more expensive than an AI agent, especially compared to some[Ruby Receptionist alternatives](https://www.quo.com/blog/ruby-receptionist-alternatives/) .


#### Ruby Receptionist pricing


**


Ruby offers 24/7 answering and bilingual support on every plan. Like Dialzara, you’ll also pay per minute for calls. Here are the bundles available:


- **50 minutes per month:** $250 per month
- **100 minutes per month:** $395 per month
- **200 minutes per month:** $720 per month
- **500 minutes per month:** $1,725 per month


### **4. Retell AI: Best AI Dialzara alternative with HIPAA compliance**


#### Pros


- Signed business associate agreement, or BAA, at no additional fee
- Outbound batch calling
- Pay as you go
- API access for custom builds


#### Cons


- Steep learning curve for teams that don’t have technical help
- Requires extensive prompt engineering


**Where it beats Dialzara:** Retell AI offers a BAA at no additional cost, which makes it suitable for healthcare practices. A BAA is required for software vendors to ensure HIPAA compliance under federal law. It also supports outbound batch campaigns per dial and per minute. Dialzara, on the other hand, sells outbound calling as a separate product, starting at $750 per month.


Retell is a developer-focused AI voice agent platform and AI-only receptionist. It can answer FAQs, transfer calls, and help book appointments. You can even add it on top of your interactive voice response, or IVR, system to help customers accomplish tasks on their own. For example, callers can securely pay invoices over the phone without a human present.


You can use Retell AI to automate outgoing calls and connect with dozens of prospects at once. For example, you could build an outbound AI agent to promote products and services to existing customers. Or the outbound agent could call happy customers and ask for a Google review or to complete an NPS® survey.


But remember that Retell is *developer* -focused, so it’s not easy to use out of the box. There’s also a[steep learning curve](https://www.g2.com/products/retell-ai/reviews/retell-ai-review-12390689) for those unfamiliar with phone AI tools. Some users also suggest that its documentation may[slow down non-technical users](https://www.g2.com/products/retell-ai/reviews/retell-ai-review-12390501) .


#### Retell AI pricing


**


Choose from one of two Retell[AI voice pricing plans](https://www.quo.com/blog/voice-ai-pricing/) :


- **Pay-as-you-go:** $0.07 to $0.31 per minute for AI voice agents, $0.002+ per message for AI chat agents, $10 worth of free credits, community support, and up to 20 concurrent calls
- **Enterprise:** Call for pricing for custom SSO, role-based access control, dedicated stable server, higher caps on concurrent calls, and 24/7 omnichannel support


### **5. Rosie AI: Best Dialzara alternative with website texting**

- Trains on your website and Google Business Profile
- Website texting add-on captures visitor details by text
- English and Spanish support are included


#### Cons


- Minute caps make monthly billing unpredictable
- Calls must be forwarded from your existing number
- Call transfers and in-call texting require a plan upgrade


**Where it beats Dialzara:** Rosie AI offers higher value from the base plan, with around 250 minutes for $49 compared to Dialzara’s 60 minutes for $29. If web chat matters to you, Rosie offers a website texting add-on.


Rosie is an AI answering service for solopreneurs and small businesses. The AI voice agent learns about your company through your website and Google Business Profile. You can add FAQs and custom instructions to fill in the gaps and teach it how to handle calls.


You can also use Rosie to manage website inquiries. Once visitors start a chat on your site, Rosie collects their name, phone number, and service request. You can review the full conversation alongside the rest of your call history.


Unfortunately, many of Rosie’s most useful features require upgrades or add-ons. For example, live appointment booking and call transfers require the $149-per-month Scale plan. Want to train your AI agent with your training docs and company policies? You’ll need to upgrade to the Growth plan, which starts at $249 per month.


But with[Rosie AI alternatives](https://www.quo.com/blog/rosie-ai-alternatives?utm_source=chatgpt.com) like Sona, these features are standard and don’t require an upgrade.


#### Rosie AI pricing


**


[Rosie AI’s pricing](https://www.quo.com/blog/rosie-ai-pricing/) plans include English and Spanish support, call summaries, and transcripts. The biggest difference is in the number of minutes you receive. Here’s what to expect:


- **Professional:** $41 per month for up to 250 minutes, custom message taking, appointment links by text, and automatic spam detection

### **6. Goodcall: Best Dialzara alternative for repeat customers**


#### Pros


- Unlimited minutes on every plan
- Predictable billing for repeat callers
- Books appointments


#### Cons


- Base plan includes one team member only
- Starter only keeps call and customer details for 30 days
- Connects to CRMs through Zapier only


**Where it beats Dialzara:** Goodcall bills per unique customer, so a repeat caller who phones 10 times only counts once. That also means long calls don’t cost extra, unlike Dialzara, which bills per minute.


Goodcall is an AI-only receptionist that can answer common questions, schedule appointments, and transfer callers to your team when necessary. You can use it full-time on your main business number or bring it in to manage overflow when your team is busy.


Keep in mind, each Goodcall AI agent needs a dedicated Goodcall number. These are separate from your existing business numbers and require you to set up[conditional call forwarding](https://www.quo.com/blog/conditional-call-forwarding/) . Unfortunately, this splits your call context across multiple numbers. It also makes it harder to track conversation histories without switching between multiple tabs.


You *might* be able to make Goodcall work if you’re a very small business with a repeat-caller base. But it won’t likely scale well as your customer base grows, which means you may need to consider a different alternative.


#### Goodcall pricing


**


Here’s how much Goodcall’s[answering service costs](https://www.quo.com/blog/answering-service-cost/) :


- **Starter:** $79 per agent per month for 100 unique callers, one team member, 30-day call history, and one external tool, plus 79¢ for each additional unique caller
- **Growth:** $129 per agent per month for 500 unique callers, five team members, 90 days of call history, and up to five external tools, plus 26¢ for each additional unique caller
- **Scale:** $299 per agent per month for 2,000 unique callers, 10 team members, unlimited call histories, and up to 15 external tools, plus 15¢ for each additional unique caller


### **7. Frontdesk AI: Best Dialzara alternative with an email AI agent**


#### Pros


- Includes voice, chat, SMS, and email support
- Comes with a built-in CRM
- Supports 20+ languages


#### Cons


- No native integrations besides API and Zapier
- Limited to 200 voice minutes per month, then overage rates apply
- Only one tier with transparent pricing


**Where it beats Dialzara:** Frontdesk AI, or My AI Front Desk, comes with 200 minutes per month compared to Dialzara’s 60 minutes. It also offers email, SMS, and chat support if you want to manage customers on various channels.


Frontdesk AI is an AI-only receptionist that lets you handle customers via calls, chats, and emails. It’s mostly designed for retail and property managers.


There are two primary ways to use Frontdesk AI:


- Purchasing and using an AI phone number from Frontdesk as your main business number
- Keeping your existing office phone number and forwarding calls to your AI phone number


Either way, you get the same basic features: access to Zapier, two agentic actions, and a log of up to 200 past customers. If you want more APIs, custom integrations, and minutes per month, you’ll need to upgrade to the Custom plan. Just keep in mind that Custom-tier pricing isn’t transparent.


You should also know that Frontdesk AI’s base plan doesn’t integrate with any other tool besides Zapier.


Last but not least, Frontdesk AI charges teams on a per-minute basis every month. It also caps your overage rate, which isn’t great for busy months or unexpected call surges.


#### Frontdesk AI pricing


**


Frontdesk AI has two pricing options:


- **Business-In-A-Box:** $79 per month for one to 10 interactions per day, 200 voice minutes per month, 400 SMS messages, and 200 webchat messages
- **Partner / Enterprise:** Custom pricing to handle 25 or more interactions per day


### **8. Ringly: Best for Shopify store owners**


#### Pros


- Native Shopify integration
- 40+ languages are supported
- 14-day free trial on the Pro plan


#### Cons


- Smaller volume sellers might struggle to justify the price
- Requires a Shopify store


**Where it beats Dialzara:** Ringly’s AI can pull order statuses and process returns through its Shopify integration. Dialzara, on the other hand, is a general-purpose receptionist.


Ringly is an[ecommerce answering service](https://www.quo.com/answering-service/ecommerce) for businesses on Shopify. Its AI agent can:


- Pull order statuses
- Process returns and exchanges
- Answer product questions from a custom knowledge base.


Ringly can also automate outbound calls. For example, it can follow up on abandoned carts and encourage shoppers to complete a purchase.


Like Frontdesk AI, you have two options for setting up Ringly’s AI agent. You can get a Ringly number or add Ringly to your existing business phone system. Either way, you have to split up context and hunt for recordings across different platforms.


Keep in mind, Ringly has a 50-call-per-month minimum. If your business handles fairly low call volume, you might want to look for a Ringly alternative.


#### Ringly pricing


**


Each Ringly interaction costs $1.99, with a minimum of $99 per month for 50 calls. If you expect to take more than 1,000 calls per month, you’ll need to speak with the sales team about a custom plan.


##


**How to switch from Dialzara**


Switching from Dialzara to a different[AI receptionist](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/receptionist) typically takes a day of setup, plus a short test period with your new provider.


Here’s how to switch from Dialzara to Quo’s Sona in five steps:


1. **Check which number callers dial.** If you forward to Dialzara using your own number, keep it by redirecting, forwarding, or porting your number to your new provider. If Dialzara issued the number, you may not be able to keep it. Check with your sales rep for more information.
2. **Rebuild your knowledge in the new tool.** With Sona, for example, you can upload documents or URLs with more information about your business. Then set escalation rules so the AI knows when to forward calls to your human reps.
3. **Run both tools side by side and test calls after hours.** Make sure to do this *before* you cancel, in case you’re unhappy with the tool or realize you forgot to upload specific knowledge to your new platform.
4. **Update call forwarding with your carrier and test from a second phone.** That way, you can hear how your receptionist sounds from a different device. This can also help you spot call quality issues, poor latency, and more.
5. **Export the recordings and transcripts you want, then cancel Dialzara.** This ensures you still have access to key recordings and conversations for legal or compliance purposes, such as GDPR.


Keep in mind that most number[ports into Quo](http://quo.com/porting) finish in seven to 14 days, depending on the carrier


💡 **Learn more** about[how porting to Quo works](https://support.quo.com/getting-started/porting/other) .


##


**Why businesses switch to Dialzara alternatives**


Here’s why Dialzara isn’t the right fit for most small and growing businesses.


### **Per-minute billing makes long calls cost more**


Your longest calls are the ones most likely to turn into revenue. Think about intakes for law firms or service bookings for HVAC or plumbing companies.


But Dialzara bills per minute, not per call. And overage fees start at $0.48 per minute on the Business Lite plan. The lowest you can pay is $0.35 per minute on the Business Elite plan, with a base rate of $349 per month.


In other words, you’ll have to budget your call time by the minute. And since you won’t know how long each customer will stay on the phone, your monthly bills can be expensive and unpredictable. This is especially true with[high call volumes](https://www.quo.com/blog/high-call-volume/) .


### **Minute allowances run out fast**


Dialzara’s Business Lite plan includes 60 minutes of calls per month. Assuming a five-minute average per call, that means you can take around 12 calls per month.


That’s likely not enough for growing businesses, even if you take a modest two to three calls per day.


### **Useful features sit behind higher plans**


Dialzara’s Lite plan may *look* affordable on the surface. But it’s only really useful as a kind of low-cost “trial.” After that, the jump to the next plan is steep. You’ll pay nearly four times more for the Dialzara Business Pro plan.


For $99, you’ll get:


- Warm transfers
- Appointment booking through calendar sync
- English and Spanish support
- After-hours rules


The Lite plan, in contrast, offers[cold transfers](https://www.quo.com/blog/warm-transfer/) only. You’ll likely outgrow it quickly as your business scales.


### **Call records live outside your phone system**


As mentioned, Dialzara only answers calls forwarded to its *own* number. That means any recordings and summaries you receive will live in Dialzara, not in your business phone system.


This can slow down your follow-up process, especially when your team has to check multiple places for conversation logs. It also increases the chances of a call slipping through the cracks.


That’s much less likely if your AI receptionist lives where you manage the rest of your calls and texts.


### **CRM syncing runs through Zapier or Make**


Dialzara *does* connect with third-party tools through Zapier and Make. But it doesn’t offer any direct integrations.


In contrast, Quo offers connections to tools you likely already use, including CRMs like Salesforce. This lets you connect your phone system to your apps without needing to set up a Zapier flow first.


##


**Switch to a Dialzara alternative today**


Dialzara *could* work as a low-cost AI voice agent for businesses with extremely low call volumes. But since it bills per minute, long calls cost more. Beyond overage costs, upgrading from the base plan comes with a steep price jump.


The best Dialzara alternatives bill per call rather than per minute. They should also answer your callers inside the phone system your team already uses — like Quo.


With Quo’s built-in AI agent, Sona, you can design an AI receptionist that fits your existing workflows. It costs a fraction of what a human receptionist would, with per-call instead of per-minute pricing. Plus, customizable call routing lets you choose how callers interact with your AI agent. You can get it up and running in 15 minutes or less.

##


**FAQs**


****How much does Dialzara cost?****


Dialzara starts at $25 per month for 60 minutes, or one hour, of calls. Any minutes used over that amount will cost $0.48. That means if you use 70 minutes in a month, you’ll pay $25 plus an additional $4.80 for the overage.


****Which Dialzara alternatives are HIPAA compliant?****


Two alternatives support HIPAA, one with human receptionists and one with AI:
– **Ruby Receptionist, human only.** Ruby offers live receptionists and HIPAA compliance. The downside is per-minute pricing that climbs fast: 500 minutes cost $1,725 a month.
– **Retell AI, AI only.** Retell offers a self-service business associate agreement, or BAA, for no additional fee. The downside is a steep learning curve for teams that don’t have existing technical expertise.


****What is the cheapest AI phone answering service?****


The “cheapest” AI phone answering service is Smith.ai with a free AI-only plan for up to 25 calls. But based on your needs, even a tool that looks cheap can end up costing more. If you take a lot of calls that are under a minute each, per-minute pricing could make sense for your team. If you take more frequent calls that tend to run longer, options with per-minute pricing like Sona might make more sense.


****Can an AI receptionist handle calls on its own?****


An AI receptionist can handle routine calls for FAQs, message taking, booking links, and lead capture. But complex, sensitive, or emergency calls need a person or a transfer rule. You can set one up in a few minutes with Sona.


****Are there any free alternatives to Dialzara?****


Yes, there are free alternatives to Dialzara, like Smith.ai. It offers 25 AI-handled calls per month for free. But keep in mind that you get what you pay for — and many of the best features require paid upgrades or add-ons.


****What is an AI receptionist service, and what services does it offer?****


An AI receptionist service is a software tool that can answer the phone 24/7, even when your human reps can’t. It can help answer FAQs, capture leads, and text booking links to callers. The full list of features depends on the service you choose.
